title: Add Journey Stitcher playground quickstart with lightweight probes
author: Maya Sinclair
description: Context: teams building multi-step retrieval-augmented flows often reimplement coordination primitives (step sequencing, fallback routing, progressive retrieval) inside their app. This quickstart introduces a compact 'Journey Stitcher' playground: a small, opinionated template that demonstrates composing RAG steps, tool-bound actions, and lightweight telemetry probes for latency and quality signals. Motivation: provide a low-friction dev loop for validating stepwise behaviors, surface latency bottlenecks early, and ship an example that shows how to wire Redwood SDK calls, local index adapters, and a minimal probe harness. This PR: - adds a playground quickstart under quickstarts/journey-stitcher - provides a typed node runner (TS) with small in-memory index stubs - includes 3 authored journey templates (faq-resolver, data-enricher, multi-pass-agent) - ships a lightweight probes library that emits token/latency samples to the console and optional JSON trace blobs - adds docs and UX notes for iterating on prompts and step contracts Checklist: - [x] scaffold quickstart and README with step-by-step dev loop - [x] add typed tool stubs and contract examples - [x] add probe harness and example traces - [x] include CI smoke e2e to run a scripted journey - [x] docs link to quickstart from /docs/quickstarts index Testing & validation: run npm ci && npm run smoke (CI job included) against a local dev token; smoke script validates token counts, step ordering, and that probes emit expected latency fields. Related: references strategy doc ENG-9372 and support ticket SUP-418 which requested a compact example to reproduce a customer multi-step failure mode. Usage notes: quickstart is intentionally small (single-file runner + two templates) to make iteration fast; it demonstrates how to replace the in-memory index with a cloud indexer or vector DB when teams are ready. Docs: added cross-links to /docs/guides/rag-playbooks and SDK examples.

release_notes: Add 'Journey Stitcher' quickstart: a compact RAG playground that demonstrates multi-step orchestration, contract-first tool stubs, and an opt-in lightweight probe harness for latency and token telemetry. Includes TS runner, three journey templates, and a CI smoke job.
notes_for_releasers: No runtime breaking changes. Quickstart is additive only. Documented env toggles for probes and CI smoke credentials. Recommend adding quickstart link to next docs site quickstarts rollup.
testing_instructions: Local: git clone && cd quickstarts/journey-stitcher && npm ci && QUICKSTART_PROBES=1 npm run smoke. CI: GitHub Actions workflow runs smoke with a test token and validates step ordering and probe emission.
extra_context: This quickstart is intentionally designed to be small enough for workshop hands-on labs and reproduces an interleaving bug reported in SUP-418 using the multi-pass-agent template. The probes are minimal by design and sized to avoid heavy telemetry ingestion costs; teams can swap in full telemetry exporters in production.
